ops.body:
REPRODUCTION FAILED 2026-08-09 (Yasyfs-MacBook-Pro / yasyf-forge, Darwin 26.6 build 25G72) — the same machine the original probe chain ran on. The stated mechanism does not hold.

DECISIVE TEST: the preserved artifact from this incident,
/opt/homebrew/Caskroom/codex-ask/1.8.4/codex-ask.provenance-wedged — the exact inode that hung
indefinitely on 2026-07-26 — now runs: 'timeout 25 ... --version' returns rc=0 and prints 1.8.4.
It STILL carries com.apple.provenance. It is byte-identical (single sha256 across both files) to the
fresh-inode replacement beside it, which also carries com.apple.provenance. Neither hangs.

Corroborating probes: (a) setting com.apple.provenance on a fresh inode and exec'ing it through a
symlink returned 0, with codesign valid and staple intact; (b) every installed cask binary on this
machine carries BOTH com.apple.provenance and com.apple.quarantine and runs — cc-present 0.31.3,
cc-review 0.33.3, cc-orchestrate 0.15.3, cc-patch 0.12.3, reposync 0.27.5, slop-cop 0.1.57.

CONCLUSION: com.apple.provenance on the inode is NOT SUFFICIENT to cause the hang. Open question #1 in
this task's own body — 'possibly a wedged syspolicyd/provenance-db state on this machine (a reboot may
clear it)' — is the surviving explanation. The wedge was machine state, since cleared by a reboot
and/or the Darwin 25.5 -> 26.6 upgrade. The fresh-inode copy did fix it in July, but because a new
inode got a NEW provenance record bypassing a wedged entry for the old one — not because provenance
per se blocks exec.

CONSEQUENCE for fix direction 3 ('homebrew-tap cask postflight xattr-strip for every daemonkit-based
cask'): a centralized fresh-inode reset was built and adversarially reviewed, but its causal comment
was wrong and is being corrected. The reset is insurance against a recurrence whose TRIGGER IS NOT
CHARACTERIZED, not a fix for a demonstrable present-day hang. Note also that the xattr-strip form was
already proven insufficient by this task's own probe chain, and that the four casks carrying it
hardcoded '#{staged_path}/binrun' while 13 of 15 casks install a differently-named artifact
(cc-orchestrate installs as 'cco'), so it was a no-op for them.

STAYS OPEN: the hang was real and cost real debugging time, and nothing here explains what wedged
syspolicyd. What is now known is that the recurrence condition is unidentified, so any fix shipped for
it is unfalsifiable until the wedge is reproduced.
